examples.ko: 별꼴이네요, 잘못은 자기가 해 놓고 오히려 화를 내요.
examples.en: What a sight, he does something wrong and then gets angry himself.
I saw all sorts of ridiculous things on the street today.
Cutting in line and even yelling is really outrageous.

examples.ko: 친구는 그 얘기를 듣고 별꼴 다 보겠다며 웃었어요.
examples.en: My friend heard the story and laughed, saying she'd seen it all now.

examples.ko: 별꼴이 다 있네요, 남의 자리에 앉아서 비키지도 않아요.
examples.en: What nerve, he's sitting in someone else's seat and won't even move.

examples.ko: 별꼴 아니에요? 자기가 낸 쓰레기를 나더러 치우래요.
examples.en: Isn't that ridiculous? He tells me to clean up the trash he made.

explain: 못마땅하거나 어이없는 사람, 행동을 보고 혼잣말처럼 자주 해요. '별꼴이야', '별꼴 다 보겠네'처럼 쓰고, 윗사람 앞에서 쓰면 무례해요. '꼴불견'은 보기 싫은 모습 자체를 말해서 조금 달라요.

phrases.example: 사과도 안 하고 오히려 화를 내다니 별꼴이에요.
phrases.en: He doesn't apologize and even gets angry, how ridiculous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어이없는 행동을 보고 못마땅해서 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when you're appalled at someone's absurd behavior.

phrases.example: 저 사람이 새치기를 하다니 별꼴 다 보겠네요.
phrases.en: He's cutting in line? What a sight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이상한 일을 다 본다는 뜻으로, 혼잣말처럼 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you've now seen everything, often said to oneself.
phrases.en_equiv: what a ridiculous thing to see

phrases.example: 공공장소에서 큰 소리로 싸우는 건 꼴불견이에요.
phrases.en: Fighting loudly in public places is an eyesore.
phrases.nuance_ko: '별꼴'과 비슷하지만 보기 싫은 모습 자체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 별꼴, but refers to the unpleasant sight itself.

explain_en: People often say it almost to themselves when they see annoying or absurd people or behavior, as in '별꼴이야' or '별꼴 다 보겠네'. It is rude to say in front of elders. '꼴불견' refers to an unpleasant sight itself, so it differs slightly.

en: to be noisy; to be in an uproar

examples.en: The classroom suddenly became rowdy.

examples.ko: 밖이 너무 소란해서 잠을 잘 수 없어요.
examples.en: It's so noisy outside that I can't sleep.
The meeting began in a commotion.
The market is always noisy but full of life.
It's noisy over there, so let's go look.
I quieted the kids who were making a racket.

explain: '시끄럽다'는 소리가 크다는 느낌이고, '소란하다'는 여러 사람이 떠들거나 일이 터져서 어수선한 분위기에 써요. 소리뿐 아니라 어지러운 상황을 말해서 '소란한 분위기'처럼 써요. '소란을 피우다'처럼 명사로도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: Before the meeting started, the atmosphere was noisy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 떠들어서 어수선한 분위기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a restless atmosphere caused by people talking.

phrases.example: 술에 취한 사람이 가게에서 소란을 피웠어요.
phrases.en: A drunk person made a scene in the shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 시끄럽게 하거나 문제를 일으킨다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests making noise or trouble, often on purpose.

phrases.example: 이 도서관은 소란하지 않아서 공부하기 좋아요.
phrases.en: This library isn't noisy, so it's good for studying.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조용하고 차분한 곳을 말할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form describes a calm, quiet place.

explain_en: Written style — disorderly uproar or commotion (교실이 소란하다) '시끄럽다' stresses loud sound, while '소란하다' suits a chaotic atmosphere when many people are making noise or something has erupted. It covers disorder, not only sound. The noun appears in '소란을 피우다' (make a scene).

t90.ax: The meeting began in a commotion.

examples.en: He devoted his whole life single-mindedly to research.

examples.ko: 외곬 성격이라서 한번 시작하면 끝까지 해요.
examples.en: I have a single-minded personality, so once I start something I finish it.

examples.ko: 한 가지 생각에만 외곬으로 빠지면 시야가 좁아져요.
examples.en: If you get stuck on one single idea, your view gets narrow.

examples.ko: 외곬인 사람은 다른 길을 잘 생각하지 못해요.
examples.en: A single-track person can't easily think of other paths.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 외곬이어서 다른 운동은 안 해 봤어요.
examples.en: That athlete is so single-minded that he has never tried other sports.

examples.ko: 너무 외곬을 고집하지 말고 다른 방법도 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't cling too much to one track; think of other ways too.

explain: 한 가지 방향으로만 나가는 것을 말해요. 좋게 말하면 한 가지에 집중하는 것이고, 나쁘게 말하면 융통성이 없는 것이에요. 발음은 '외곬이[외골씨]', '외곬으로[외골쓰로]'처럼 달라지니 조심하세요.

phrases.example: 한 가지만 외곬으로 생각하면 답을 못 찾아요.
phrases.en: If you think about only one thing, you can't find the answer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 가지 방향으로만 생각한다는 뜻이고, 조금 나쁜 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means thinking in one direction only, with a slightly negative feel.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 외곬 성격이라서 융통성이 없어요.
phrases.en: That friend has a one-track personality, so he is not flexible.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 가지에만 매달리는 성격을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a personality that sticks to one thing only.

phrases.example: 그는 한 가지 연구에만 외곬으로 파고들었어요.
phrases.en: He dug into just one piece of research single-mindedly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 가지 일에만 깊이 매달릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone commits deeply to just one thing.

explain_en: It means going in only one direction. Positively it means focusing on one thing; negatively it means being inflexible. Watch the pronunciation changes: '외곬이' is [외골씨] and '외곬으로' is [외골쓰로].

t90.ax: He devoted his whole life single-mindedly to research.

examples.en: Please don't speak so heartlessly.

examples.ko: 인정머리 없는 사장 밑에서 일하기 힘들어요.
examples.en: It's hard to work under a heartless boss.

examples.ko: 저 사람은 인정머리가 너무 없다고 소문났어요.
examples.en: He's known for having no warmth at all.

examples.ko: 아픈 친구를 두고 가다니 인정머리도 없네요.
examples.en: Leaving a sick friend behind—how heartless.
She's a teacher known for being cold-hearted.
How can you refuse so heartlessly?

explain: '인정'보다 거칠고 나무라는 말투라서 '인정머리 없다'처럼 거의 부정문으로 써요. 상대를 비난하는 느낌이 있으니 윗사람에게 직접 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.

phrases.en: I don't want to be misunderstood as a heartless person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 비난할 때 가장 흔한 꼴이니 직접 대놓고 쓰지는 마세요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form for criticizing someone; avoid saying it directly to a person.

phrases.example: 어떻게 그렇게 인정머리 없이 거절할 수 있어요?
phrases.en: How could you turn them down so coldly?
phrases.nuance_ko: 행동하는 방식이 차갑고 매정하다는 뜻으로 부사처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used like an adverb for acting in a cold, unfeeling way.

phrases.en: That person has not a shred of warmth.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-라곤 없다'를 붙이면 '조금도 없다'는 뜻이 되어 더 강하게 나무라요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -라곤 없다 means 'not even a bit', making the criticism stronger.
phrases.en_equiv: to have no warmth at all

explain_en: Spoken, critical — usually in negatives about cold people (인정머리가 없다) It sounds rougher and more scolding than '인정', so it is used almost only in negatives like '인정머리 없다'. Since it criticizes the other person, avoid saying it directly to someone senior.

en: to be petty; to be stingy; to be cheap

examples.en: Getting that angry over so little is really petty.

examples.ko: 밥값 몇천 원을 따지는 건 쪼잔하지 않아요?
examples.en: Isn't it petty to argue over a few thousand won for a meal?
My friend acted so petty that I felt hurt.

examples.ko: 쪼잔한 사람처럼 보이고 싶지 않아서 그냥 냈어요.
examples.en: I didn't want to look petty, so I just paid.

examples.ko: 우리 팀장님은 쪼잔해서 커피 한 잔도 안 사 줘요.
examples.en: Our team leader is so stingy he won't even buy us a coffee.
I guess I was a bit petty back then.

explain: 작은 돈이나 사소한 일에 인색하고 마음이 좁을 때 쓰는 구어체 말이에요. 친구끼리는 농담처럼 쓰지만 윗사람이나 처음 만난 사람에게 쓰면 무례해요. 비슷한 말로 '치사하다'가 있고, 반대로 마음이 넓은 사람은 '통이 크다'고 해요.

phrases.example: 쪼잔한 사람이랑은 같이 여행 가기 싫어요.
phrases.en: I don't want to travel with a petty person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사소한 일에 마음이 좁고 인색한 사람을 말해요. 친한 사이에서 쓰는 거친 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a person who is narrow-minded and stingy about small things. It's rough language for close friends.

phrases.example: 쪼잔하게 굴지 말고 한번 사 주세요.
phrases.en: Don't be petty, buy me one just this once.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사소한 일에 인색하게 행동하는 것을 말해요. 친구끼리 농담처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means acting stingy over small things. Friends use it jokingly.

phrases.en: It's petty of you to argue about that.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말로, 비겁하거나 인색한 행동이 마음에 안 들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word, used when you dislike someone's mean or stingy behavior.

explain_en: Very casual slang for petty or stingy behavior (과자 한 개) This is a colloquial word for being stingy or small-minded about little money or trivial matters. Friends use it jokingly, but it is rude toward elders or people you just met. A similar word is '치사하다', and the opposite idea is '통이 크다' (to be generous and big-hearted).

t90.ax: I guess I was a bit petty back then.

examples.ko: 우리 강아지는 아직 천방지축이라서 산책이 힘들어요.
examples.en: Our puppy is still wild, so walks are hard.
The kids are running around wildly, so it's chaotic.
Even our youngest, who used to be a wild one, has become much more mature.

examples.ko: 천방지축인 동생 때문에 늘 마음을 졸여요.
examples.en: I'm always anxious because of my reckless younger sibling.
I was a wild child too during my teens.

examples.ko: 천방지축 뛰어다니지 말고 좀 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: Stop running around like crazy and sit down for a bit.

explain: 철없이 마구 날뛰거나 덤비는 모습을 말해요. '천방지축 날뛰다', '천방지축이다'처럼 쓰고, 어린아이나 강아지에게 애정을 담아 말하기도 해요. 어른에게 쓰면 흉보는 말이 돼요.

phrases.en: The calf is running wild.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정신없이 마구 뛰는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for frantic, uncontrolled running around.

phrases.en: It's tiring looking after a child who is so unruly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 철없이 마구 구는 아이를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a child who acts heedlessly.

phrases.en: If you act recklessly, you could get hurt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각 없이 막 행동할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for acting without thinking.

explain_en: It describes acting wild and heedless, without thinking. People say '천방지축 날뛰다' or '천방지축이다', and use it affectionately about kids or puppies. Said about an adult, it becomes criticism.

examples.en: The job market is not easy these days.

examples.ko: 서울에서 혼자 사는 일이 녹록지 않았어요.
examples.en: Living alone in Seoul wasn't easy.
If you take that team lightly, you will get burned.

examples.ko: 처음 하는 장사가 녹록할 리가 없지요.
examples.en: A first-time business can't possibly be easy.

examples.ko: 요즘 경기가 나빠서 장사가 녹록지 않다고 해요.
examples.en: They say business isn't easy because the economy is bad these days.

examples.ko: 세상살이는 녹록한 게 아니라고 어머니가 늘 말씀하세요.
examples.en: My mother always says that life in this world is not a pushover.

explain: '녹록하지 않다'처럼 부정 표현과 함께 써서 '쉽지 않다, 만만치 않다'라는 뜻으로 말하는 경우가 많아요. 줄이면 '녹록지 않다'가 맞는 표기예요. 상황이나 사람이 만만하다는 뜻이라 사람에게 쓰면 '순해서 다루기 쉬운'이라는 뜻이 되기도 해요.

phrases.en: Making ends meet is not easy these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: '녹록하지 않아요'의 줄임말로, 상황이 만만하지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A contracted form of '녹록하지 않아요', used when a situation is not easy.

phrases.example: 녹록하지 않은 현실이지만 포기하지 않을 거예요.
phrases.en: It is a tough reality, but I won't give up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사를 붙여 '쉽지 않은 ~'라는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attached before a noun to mean 'a not-easy ~'.

phrases.en: Life studying abroad was not easy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지난 일이 쉽지 않았다고 말할 때 쓰는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past tense, used to say that something was not easy.

explain_en: It is often used with a negative, as in '녹록하지 않다', to mean 'not easy' or 'not a pushover'. The correct shortened spelling is '녹록지 않다'. It describes a situation or person as easy to handle, and said of a person it can mean 'meek and easy to deal with'.

t90.ax: Living alone in Seoul wasn't easy.

examples.ko: 그는 본업이 의사이고 취미로 노래를 해요.
examples.en: His main job is doctor, and he sings as a hobby.
These days my side job is busier than my main job.
I couldn't rest because I focused on my main job.
Singing is his main job, but he also acts.
I quit my main job and opened a shop.
It's hard to do my main job and child care together.

explain: 본업은 부업과 짝으로 쓰는 말이고, 가장 중심이 되는 직업이에요. 학생에게는 '본분'이라는 말을 써서 공부가 본분이라고 해요. 직업을 물을 때는 '본업이 뭐예요?'보다 '무슨 일을 하세요?'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I'm busy because I do both my main job and a side job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짝말인 '부업'과 함께 쓰는 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use, paired with '부업'.

phrases.example: 그는 본업이 따로 있고 주말에만 가수로 일해요.
phrases.en: He has a main job elsewhere and sings only on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주로 하는 일이 다른 곳에 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say one's main work is something else.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a separate main job

phrases.en: I want to focus on my main job now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 일보다 중심이 되는 일에 힘쓴다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means putting effort into the central job over other things.
phrases.en_equiv: to focus on one's main job

explain_en: 본업 pairs with 부업 (side job) and means the central occupation. For students people use 본분, saying that studying is their 본분. When asking someone's job, 무슨 일을 하세요? sounds more natural than 본업이 뭐예요?

examples.en: A good environment helps a child grow.
That experience made me grow.
I want to grow the company big.
I am looking for ways to develop my skills.
Sunlight is important for growing plants.
They grew a small shop into a chain.

explain: '자라다'는 스스로 크는 것이고 '성장시키다'는 누군가가 키우거나 발전시키는 것이에요. 회사, 실력, 경제처럼 추상적인 것에도 써요. 사람이 크는 일은 '키우다'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: My parents raised me well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 자라는 일에는 '성장시키다'보다 이 말을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For people growing up, this is used more than 성장시키다.

phrases.en: I improve my skills by practicing every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실력이나 기술을 더 좋게 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means making skills or technology better.

phrases.en: A new product makes the company grow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사나 경제 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation in talk about companies and the economy.

explain_en: Cause a person, company or plant to grow bigger. The intransitive verb is growing by itself; this one is making something grow or develop. It works for abstract things like a company, skill or economy. For raising children, the plain verb for raising is more common.

dis.h: make a company or person develop and grow
gh: grow crops or plants on purpose

p.n: 재배하다 means growing crops or plants, so it cannot replace this sentence.

en: to end a semester; to finish the course

examples.en: Our class ends next week.
The professor finished the course with today's class.
When the semester ends, the library becomes quiet.
When did your classes end that you're so free?
The day the course ends is different for each subject.
Some lectures ended early.

explain: 반대말은 '개강하다'예요. 주어로 '수업, 강의, 학교, 교수님'이 자연스럽게 와요. 학기의 마지막 수업이 끝났을 때 쓰는 말이라서 하루 수업이 끝나는 것에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: Our school's semester ended yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형이에요. 학기가 이미 끝났다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the past tense, saying the semester has already ended.

phrases.en: When the semester ends, I'll go home right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)면'으로 학기가 끝난 뒤의 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -(으)면 it introduces what happens once the semester ends.

phrases.en: On the last day of class, the teacher gave us snacks.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 날을 꾸며요. '종강 날'과 비슷해요.
phrases.nuance_en: -는 modifies 날, which is close to 종강 날.

explain_en: Only for a semester or course finishing its last class (학원이 종강하다). Its opposite is '개강하다'. Natural subjects are a class, a lecture, a school or a professor. It means the last class of the term is over, so it isn't used for a single day's lesson ending.

examples.en: I entered the university this year as a transfer student.

examples.ko: 편입생은 학점 인정 절차를 먼저 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: Transfer students need to check the credit recognition process first.

examples.ko: 우리 반에 편입생이 두 명 있어요.
examples.en: There are two transfer students in our class.
An information session for transfer students is being held.
My transfer student friend says the school still feels unfamiliar.
Some schools give scholarships to transfer students.

explain: 주로 대학에서 다른 학교나 학과에서 옮겨 온 학생을 말해요. 초·중·고등학교에서는 보통 '전학생'이라고 하고, 처음 입학한 학생은 '신입생'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I transferred to this university last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '편입생'이 사람이라면 '편입하다'는 다른 학교에서 옮겨 들어오는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: While 'transfer student' names the person, this verb describes the act of moving in from another school.

phrases.en: Many departments are recruiting transfer students this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학 공지에서 자주 보이는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in university announcements.

phrases.en: I'm a transfer student who joined this semester.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기소개할 때 '이에요'를 붙여서 신분을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when introducing yourself and stating your status.

explain_en: It mainly refers to a student who moved into a university from another school or major. In elementary through high school, people usually say '전학생', and a first-time entrant is a '신입생'.

t90.ax: There are two transfer students in our class.

en: to be cold; to be chilly; to be frosty

examples.en: My uncle answered in a cold tone.

examples.ko: 싸운 뒤로 집 안 분위기가 냉랭해요.
examples.en: Since the fight, the mood at home has been frosty.
The boss's face was cold from the morning, which was scary.

examples.ko: 두 사람 사이가 냉랭해진 지 오래됐어요.
examples.en: It has been a long time since the two grew cold toward each other.
I greeted them, but the response was cold.
I was hurt by the cold attitude.

explain: 온도보다 분위기, 말투, 표정, 사이가 차가울 때 많이 써요. '쌀쌀하다'는 날씨에도 쓰지만 '냉랭하다'는 주로 사람 쪽 이야기에 어울리고, 반대로는 '다정하다'가 있어요.

phrases.en: We ate dinner in a chilly atmosphere.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들 사이의 차가운 분위기를 말할 때 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to describe a cold atmosphere between people.

phrases.en: Things between the two of them have been cold lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사이가 차갑게 식었을 때 해요체로 말하는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for saying that a relationship has turned cold.

phrases.en: He treated me coldly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차갑고 무뚝뚝한 태도로 사람을 대할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone treats a person with a cold, curt attitude.

explain_en: Cold atmosphere or manner between people; formal. It is mostly used for a cold mood, tone, expression or relationship rather than temperature. '쌀쌀하다' also works for weather, but '냉랭하다' suits talk about people, and the opposite is '다정하다'.

t90.ax: I was hurt by the cold attitude.

examples.en: A stream of water pours down the mountain.
The water from the shower is too weak.
The firefighter sprayed a jet of water at the fire.
The course of this river runs all the way to the sea.
The sound of the waterfall is very loud.
The gardener sprays a thin stream of water on the flowers.

explain: 이름이 있는 큰 흐름은 '강'이고, 수도꼭지·호스·폭포에서 가늘고 길게 나오는 물에도 '물줄기'를 써요. '물줄기가 세다/약하다', '물줄기를 뿜다'처럼 말해요. 강이 흘러가는 길을 말할 때는 '물길'도 써요.

phrases.en: The water stream was strong, so my clothes got soaked.
phrases.nuance_ko: '세다'는 힘이 강하다는 뜻이라 물이 힘차게 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 세다 means strong, so it describes water coming out forcefully.

phrases.en: The fountain shoots a stream of water high.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 힘 있게 위로 나오는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes water shooting out with force.

phrases.en: I walked along the waterway.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물줄기는 나오는 물이고, 물길은 물이 흘러가는 길이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 물줄기 is the stream of water itself; 물길 is the path the water flows along.

explain_en: A big named flow is a '강', but '물줄기' is also used for the thin, long line of water from a faucet, a hose or a waterfall. You say '물줄기가 세다/약하다' and '물줄기를 뿜다'. For the path a river takes, '물길' is also used.

examples.en: I walked down a road where cosmos swayed in the autumn breeze.
The puppy greeted me, wagging its tail.
The wind chime by the window tinkled lightly and woke me up.
Now that spring is here, the willow branches sway gently.

examples.ko: 열어 둔 창문 때문에 커튼이 밤새 살랑댔어요.
examples.en: Because I left the window open, the curtain swayed all night.
Every time the breeze stirs, I smell the flowers.

explain: '살랑거리다'와 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 활용이 '살랑대요, 살랑댔어요, 살랑대는'처럼 짧고 간단해요.

phrases.en: The spring breeze is blowing gently, so I feel good.
phrases.nuance_ko: '살랑대다'와 뜻이 같고, '거리다' 모양이 조금 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '살랑대다'; the '거리다' form is a bit more common.

phrases.en: The fluttering skirt hem is pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '살랑대는' 모양으로 뒤에 오는 말을 꾸밀 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '살랑대는' form can describe the noun that follows.

phrases.en: Yesterday the breeze was blowing gently.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지난 일을 말하는 해요체 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite past form for talking about something that already happened.

explain_en: It means the same as '살랑거리다' and can replace it. Its conjugations are short and simple: '살랑대요', '살랑댔어요', '살랑대는'.

t90.ax: The puppy greeted me, wagging its tail.
